newsitem.title: UK: UK picks bank, building soc bidders for loan funds.
newsitem.headline: UK picks bank, building soc bidders for loan funds.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it had shortlisted four bidders in the proposed privatisation of government loans to UK housing associations.
In a statement, Environment Minister John Gummer said the government planned to proceed with the sale "subject to receiving satisfactory final bids at the conclusion of negotiations".

Four parties have been asked to submit final bids, including one building society consortium whose members include Abbey National Treasury Services, Halifax and Nationwide Building Societies, with Hambros Bank Ltd.

Two other groups -- NatWest Markets, a unit of National Westminster Bank, and a consortium comprised of The Housing Finance Corp and banks, Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Barclays Plc and Bank of Scotland -- have also bid for all the loans available under the sell-off.
A fourth bidder, The Principality Mortgage Corporation Limited, has prequalified only for the loans held by the Housing of Wales association.
Combined, the loan portfolios have a book value of about 970 million stg.

Charles Keay, executive director of NM Rothschild & Sons which is handling the sale for the government, said it was expected that the loans would be sold "at a substantial premium to their book value".
This was because of the high fixed rate of interest they bear, the substantial security cover afforded and their excellent arrears performance, he added.
